User guide

This guide covers the two questions most users ask when first reaching for MIND:

  1. How do I format my own data?

  2. Which hyperparameters should I tune, and to what?

It complements the autogenerated API reference.

1. Input format

MIND.MIND accepts a single argument, data_dict, which is a Python dictionary mapping a modality name to a pandas.DataFrame. The DataFrames must satisfy:

Property

Requirement

Row count

Identical across all modalities.

Row index

Aligned across modalities — row i of RNA and row i of methyl must refer to the same patient.

Missingness

Patients missing from a modality are encoded as a row of all-NaN. Partially-observed rows are not supported and will raise ValueError.

Dtype

Numeric (float).

Scale

Approximately z-scored (zero mean, unit variance per feature) is strongly recommended — MIND assumes a standard-Normal prior on the latent space.

Example:

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

rna = pd.read_csv("rna.csv", index_col=0)
methyl = pd.read_csv("methyl.csv", index_col=0)

# Align indices: outer-join, then set rows that are missing in one
# modality to NaN.
all_patients = rna.index.union(methyl.index)
rna = rna.reindex(all_patients)
methyl = methyl.reindex(all_patients)

# Z-score per modality, ignoring NaNs.
def zscore(df):
    obs = ~df.isna().all(axis=1)
    arr = df.values.copy()
    arr[obs] = StandardScaler().fit_transform(arr[obs])
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=df.index, columns=df.columns)

rna = zscore(rna)
methyl = zscore(methyl)

data_dict = {"RNA": rna, "methyl": methyl}

The package validates the dictionary structure at construction time (MIND._validation.validate_data_dict) — common mistakes raise descriptive errors immediately rather than producing silent NaN losses later.

2. Hyperparameters

Argument

Default

What it controls

When to tune

emb_dim

128

Latent embedding dimensionality.

Set to 16–32 for visualisation; 64–128 for downstream prediction with large datasets.

lr (passed to my_train)

1e-3

Adam learning rate.

Lower (1e-4) if loss oscillates; higher rarely helps.

n_epoch (passed to my_train)

2000

Number of optimisation epochs.

Watch the loss curve — most datasets plateau by 1k–3k epochs.

alpha

5e-2

Weight of the modality-alignment penalty (pull per-modality embeddings of the same patient together).

Increase (0.1–1.0) when modalities give wildly different embeddings; decrease (1e-3) when you want each modality to retain idiosyncratic signal.

beta

1.0

Strength of the t-SNE neighbourhood-preservation term.

Rarely changed. Lower it (0.1) if the embedding looks over-clustered.

perp

30

Perplexity for the per-modality nearest-neighbour graph. Same role as t-SNE perplexity.

Pass a list to use a different value per modality. Lower (10) for smaller datasets (<200 patients).

batch_size (in my_train)

None

Mini-batch size. None means full-batch (the paper default).

Set to e.g. 256 only for very large patient counts where full-batch training exhausts memory.

device

'cpu'

PyTorch device string.

'cuda' if you have a GPU.

Suggested workflow for a new dataset:

  1. Verify input format by constructing the model — validation errors will point at any structural problems.

  2. Train for ~100 epochs at the defaults to make sure the loss decreases.

  3. Train for the full 2000 epochs.

  4. Plot get_embedding()[0] (after PCA or TSNE) and inspect cluster structure. If embeddings are degenerate, lower alpha and re-train.

3. Outputs

get_embedding() returns a tuple (z_mean, z_log_std) of shape (n_patients, emb_dim). For most downstream tasks z_mean is what you want; z_log_std quantifies per-patient posterior uncertainty.

predict() returns a list of per-modality reconstruction tensors. For patients originally missing in a modality, this is the model’s prediction of what their values would have been.

4. Reproducing the paper

python examples/reproduce_results.py --dataset CCMA

The script downloads the data on first run, trains MIND with the paper’s hyperparameters, and writes the embeddings + clinical labels to ./MIND_outputs/.
